method: Desk research from official repositories and documentation, plus Battleships (built by the boat.dev team) as a secondary source for workload shape and duty cycle. No account, sandbox, or purchase was used.
caveats: Battleships presets are fleet-scale. Use their per-machine shape and cpuUtil, then scale the machine count.
Battleships idleShare is published but undefined in its public guide, so it is recorded but not interpreted.
Prices are USD list prices on 2026-10-29 and can change.
not_found means the pages inspected did not state it; it is not proof that the capability does not exist.

use_cases.name: Hermes Agent
use_cases.what_it_is: An open-source (MIT) personal AI agent by Nous Research that runs on a server you control, talks through 20+ chat platforms, keeps memory, and writes reusable skills.

minimum.note: Hermes Docker guide: 1 GB RAM, 1 core, 500 MB data volume. Browser tools raise the RAM floor to 2 GB.

recommended.note: Hermes Docker guide: 2 cores, 2-4 GB RAM, 2+ GB disk. The 2+ GB disk grows with sessions and skills.

use_cases.always_on_detail: Telegram long polling is outbound and cannot sleep. Webhook mode plus a host that auto-wakes on inbound HTTP can sleep between messages, but cron jobs do not fire while asleep.
use_cases.inbound: Chat platform adapters (long polling by default; webhook optional). External events can use the HTTP webhook adapter.

battleships.description: Assistant agents that each live on their own machine all the time (one per employee or customer, like OpenClaw or Hermes): they keep their memory and files, hold logins to your tools, answer messages, run scheduled jobs and use a browser.
battleships.note: 50 machines on 24/7 is a fleet preset, not one person. The per-machine shape is 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 20 GiB.

proposed_workload.reasoning: Vendor recommendation is 2 cores / 2-4 GB / 2+ GB; browser tools need at least 2 GB. 4 GiB and 20 GiB give room for Chromium, skills and sessions. 730 hours is 24/7 for a polling gateway with cron. minimum.note: Claude Code requires 4 GB+ RAM and an x64 or ARM64 processor. It does not publish a CPU-count or disk floor. OpenAI does not publish Codex CLI requirements in the pages inspected.

recommended.note: Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions use approximate ceilings of 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM and 30 GB disk. Battleships fullstack uses 4 vCPU / 8 GiB / 20 GiB.

battleships.name: Software factory
battleships.description: Agents that build and ship software, each on its own machine for a work session of about 8 hours: Docker for services and test databases, a desktop and a browser to check the UI they built, and a disk that keeps the work between sessions.
battleships.note: 2,200 eight-hour sessions a month at 100 concurrent is a software-factory fleet. Use the per-machine shape and duty cycle for one developer.

proposed_workload.reasoning: Claude Code needs 4 GB+ RAM. 8 GiB covers the CLI, a language server, tests and a couple of containers; 40 GiB leaves room for Docker images and caches that the 20 GiB preset does not. 160 hours is 8 h x 20 workdays. Battleships averages 3.4% CPU with a 47% peak.

team_variant.reasoning: One sandbox per developer. Claude Code is not built for multiple tenants: it keeps state on disk and its tools change files on the machine it runs on.

use_cases.name: Code interpreter inside your own product
use_cases.what_it_is: A sandbox your application calls to run user or LLM code, returning stdout, errors and files. It is infrastructure you embed, not a product your users log into.

minimum.note: Provider floors vary: Modal 0.125 core / 128 MiB, E2B default 2 vCPU / 512 MiB, Daytona 1 vCPU / 1 GiB / 3 GiB. 1 vCPU / 512 MiB / 1 GiB is the practical floor.

recommended.note: Battleships interp uses 1 vCPU / 2 GiB / 5 GiB and records 81.5% RAM utilisation, so 4 GiB is the safer general-purpose size.

use_cases.always_on_detail: Each run is short-lived. E2B defaults to a 5-minute timeout and kills the sandbox; Vercel Sandbox also defaults to 5 minutes.
use_cases.inbound: Your app receives the request and calls the sandbox API. The sandbox needs no public inbound webhook; E2B public URLs can be restricted with allowPublicTraffic: false.
persists: Optional: E2B pause/snapshot or volume; Vercel persistent sandboxes; Daytona snapshots
Return output files to your own object storage

battleships.name: Code interpreter bursts
battleships.description: An AI app that runs short pieces of code for its users: lots of one-minute runs, each on a small machine.
battleships.note: 200,000 one-minute runs a month at 100 concurrent. RAM is the binding resource at 2 GiB.

proposed_workload.machines_note: concurrent pool; 20,000 short-lived runs a month
proposed_workload.reasoning: The 1 vCPU / 2 GiB / 5 GiB preset is the floor and is already 81.5% RAM-utilised. 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 10 GiB gives headroom for Python libraries and temporary files. 20,000 one-minute runs is about 650 a day; a 10-machine pool absorbs bursts. Outputs go to object storage, so no persistent disk.

use_cases.name: Browser or computer-use agent
use_cases.what_it_is: An agent that drives a real browser (open pages, read the DOM or a screenshot, click, type, fill forms), or a whole desktop with a virtual display, mouse and keyboard.

minimum.note: Battleships browseruse preset is 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 10 GiB; Browserless minimum is 2 cores / 4 GB; Steel requires 4 GB RAM and 10 GB disk.

recommended.note: For browser-only work, the 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 10 GiB minimum is enough. For a full desktop, Battleships cua uses 4 vCPU / 8 GiB / 20 GiB. Anthropic does not publish CPU/RAM/disk sizing for computer use.

use_cases.always_on_detail: Sessions are task-scoped, about 10 minutes for browser use and 15 minutes for computer use in Battleships. Only a saved browser profile or cookies need to persist.
use_cases.inbound: Your app or agent loop sends a goal or action and receives a screenshot or DOM snapshot. No inbound chat webhook unless you add one.
persists: Optional: browser profile, cookies and local storage if logins must survive

battleships.name: Browser-use agents
battleships.description: Agents that do tasks on websites for your users: open a real browser, read the page, click and fill forms. Sessions of about 10 minutes.
battleships.note: 30,000 ten-minute sessions a month at 50 concurrent.

proposed_workload.reasoning: Exact Battleships browser-use shape and Browserless minimum. 30,000 ten-minute sessions is about 1,000 a day; 50 concurrent at peak. CPU is not the constraint; each Chromium instance is memory-hungry. Persist a profile only if logins must survive.

computer_use_variant.audience: small team needing a full desktop
computer_use_variant.reasoning: A full desktop adds Xvfb, a window manager, VNC and a browser. Battleships cua preset doubles the shape to 4 vCPU / 8 GiB / 20 GiB. Daytona default 1 vCPU / 1 GiB / 3 GiB is a code-sandbox default, not a desktop default.
